slides.sub: Sheffield 1989. The night Warp Records made electronic music into art.

text: Sheffield became a city left behind.
The dark of those empty factories
slides.sub: Abandoned industry. A sound born from inside its walls.

text: Two years later, they pressed a single.
slides.sub: First release: Forgemasters, Track with No Name. 1989.
Gez Varley and Mark Bell. Leeds. The record that kept Warp alive.

slides.note: Warp, 1992. Artificial Intelligence. Aphex Twin, Autechre, Richie Hawtin, B12. The birth of IDM. Electronic music that refused the dance floor.

text: Aphex Twin: Selected Ambient Works II. 1994.
Music Has The Right To Children. 1998.
slides.sub: Not singles. Albums. Not one night. A lifetime. That was Warp's philosophy.

text: Co-founder. Half the soul of Warp.
slides.sub: Flying Lotus. Oneohtrix Point Never. Battles. Warp kept moving forward.

slides.strobe: The city the world abandoned made the most enduring electronic music ever released.
